title: Signal Smokestack: compact patch docket and probe notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
A compact working log of recent customer signals that cluster around runtime friction, small API ergonomics, and rollout surprises. This is intentionally a lightweight artifact for fast handoffs to Eng/Prod Ops and for seeding 1–2 week probes. Not a canonical synthesis — consider it a smoke-test of priorities.

Topline: three microthemes surfaced repeatedly
1) KV/prefix cache correctness & observability — multiple customers report stale completions or hallucination spikes after cache warmups.
2) Burst latency cliffs — predictable under small-burst concurrency (5–20 rps) on Dedicated pools; customers expect consistent p95 but see transient regressions after autoscale events.
3) API ergonomics for streaming + tool-calls — edge cases where function call boundary events interleave with partial-stream events and cause client retries.

Representative vignettes (raw customer quotes preserved):
- "We see coherent answers for 30–60 tokens then suddenly it derails — looks like kv cache got out of sync when we switch temperature between calls." — Enterprise fintech POC
- "During lunch the model p95 jumps to 700ms for a few minutes; our dashboards show a small spike in pod restarts on the worker pool." — Mid-market SaaS using Dedicated
- "If we call the search tool mid-stream the client sometimes receives two tool outputs (duplicated) causing our de-dup step to choke." — AI-native startup

Quick triage matrix (impact / cost / immediate ask):
- KV cache correctness
  * Impact: High (affects correctness and trust)
  * Effort: Medium (diagnostics + small runtime fix)
  * Immediate ask: Add KV-cache version header in streams and logs; instrument prefix mismatches (Jira: JIRA-CS-4321).
- Burst latency cliffs
  * Impact: Medium-High (SLA complaints)
  * Effort: Medium-Large (root cause may be autoscaler/hot-restart behavior)
  * Immediate ask: Canary autoscale policy variation (reduce hot-restarts, add warm buffer).
- Streaming/tool-call duplication
  * Impact: Medium (integration complexity for clients)
  * Effort: Small
  * Immediate ask: Add a stream boundary flag + sample client library patch to dedupe on idempotency keys.

Candidate small patches (can be adopted by Eng with low risk):
1) Log shim that emits per-request: model-version, kv-cache-revision, prefix-length, first-token-time, last-token-time. (S) — helps correlate hallucination windows. Owner: Benji Ramos.
2) Add stream header "x-rw-prefix-id" returned in initial websocket/stream frame so SDKs can assert prefix continuity. (M) — prevents inadvertent mismatch after prefetch. Owner: Priya Nair.
3) Streaming SDK example: opt-in dedupe via per-tool-call UUID and a recommended backoff pattern for partial-stream retries. (S) — repo PR: linked above. Owner: Marisol Chen.

Proposed probes (1–3 week experiments):
- Probe A: Autoscale warm-buffer experiment on a single Dedicated customer pool (select low-risk tenant). Increase pre-warmed standby nodes by 20% and measure p95 during simulated lunch-burst profile. KPIs: p95 latency, pod restart rate, cost delta. Expected outcome: confirm whether warm buffer reduces cliffs.
- Probe B: KV-cache verifiability rollout. Add a cache-rev header and passive telemetry; run for 2 weeks in hosted to measure mismatch events per million requests. KPIs: mismatch rate, correlated hallucination incidents.

Risk & open questions (notes to self):
- Could adding headers to streaming frames impact throughput? Need microbenchmark (Benji).
- Some customers might not want extra metadata for compliance; design headers opt-in per-tenant.
- Is duplication in tool-calls client-side or server-side? Initial triage points both; we need end-to-end traces. Ask SRE to add trace sampling for events where client submits retry within stream window.

Short-term customer comms draft (for CS to send):
"Hi — thanks for flagging this. We have prioritized a low-risk diagnostic rollout that will add additional per-request metadata to help us pinpoint prefix/caching issues. We expect no downtime and will share findings within 10 business days. If you prefer not to receive extra metadata in responses, reply and we will opt you out."

Execution notes and owners:
- Diagnostics shim (logs + header): Benji — due 2028-09-21 (internal diag-only rollout).
- SDK dedupe example + docs: Marisol & DX — due 2028-09-25 (publish sample code and a short how-to).
- Autoscale warm-buffer canary: Eng infra + SRE (Diego) — plan doc by 2028-09-22, canary start 2028-09-25.

Follow-ups for next pass (what to fold into a heavier synthesis):
- Collect all related Jira keys for prior cache incidents and collapse duplicates.
- Run a 72-hour log merge for tenants with reported hallucination spikes and search for commonalities (model families, quantization settings, sequence-length distribution).
- Reach out to two customers willing to run a controlled experiment (one Hosted, one Dedicated).

Appendix: quick links and artifacts referenced
- Confluence: Signal Smokestack landing page (design notes + probe templates) — https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/Signal+Smokestack+Landing
- Related PR: runtime behavior probe (github) — https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/238
- Triage ticket (aggregated): JIRA-CS-4321

Last note (unpolished):
- Might be useful to add short prescriptive guidance for customers using large prefixes: "If you warm a prefix and then change hyperparameters between calls, re-derive kv cache or start a fresh session." Add that to the SDK FAQ as a short blurb.

-- end of compact docket, saved as working doc for quick handoffs.
